name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.number || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.run_id || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' }}

jobs:
  pre-commit:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/pre-commit-hooks.yaml

  python:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/test_py.yaml

  typescript:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/test_ts.yaml

  go:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/test_go.yaml

  rust:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/test_rust.yaml

  release-artifacts:
    name: Build and verify release artifacts
    needs: [pre-commit, python, typescript, go, rust]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12.13"

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@d0cc045d04ccac9d8b7881df0226f9e82c39688e # v6
        with:
          version: "0.10.6"
          enable-cache: false

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4
        with:
          version: 10.33.2

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4cda84d5c5c54efe2404f9d843567869ab1699d4 # stable
        with:
          toolchain: 1.97.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: 22.23.1
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: abxbus-ts/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Build Python and npm distributions once
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          rm -rf release-artifacts abxbus-ts/dist
          mkdir -p release-artifacts/python release-artifacts/npm release-artifacts/cratesio
          uv build --out-dir release-artifacts/python
          rm -f release-artifacts/python/.gitignore
          pnpm --dir abxbus-ts install --frozen-lockfile
          pnpm --dir abxbus-ts run build
          pnpm --dir abxbus-ts pack --pack-destination "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-artifacts/npm"
          cargo package --locked --manifest-path abxbus-rust/Cargo.toml
          crate=(abxbus-rust/target/package/abxbus-*.crate)
          [[ "${#crate[@]}" -eq 1 ]]
          cp "${crate[0]}" release-artifacts/cratesio/

          shopt -s nullglob
          wheels=(release-artifacts/python/abxbus-*.whl)
          sdists=(release-artifacts/python/abxbus-*.tar.gz)
          npm_packages=(release-artifacts/npm/abxbus-*.tgz)
          crates=(release-artifacts/cratesio/abxbus-*.crate)
          [[ "${#wheels[@]}" -eq 1 ]]
          [[ "${#sdists[@]}" -eq 1 ]]
          [[ "${#npm_packages[@]}" -eq 1 ]]
          [[ "${#crates[@]}" -eq 1 ]]
          [[ "$(find release-artifacts/python -maxdepth 1 -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -eq 2 ]]
          [[ "$(find release-artifacts/npm -maxdepth 1 -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -eq 1 ]]
          printf '%s\n' "$GITHUB_SHA" > release-artifacts/COMMIT_SHA
          (
            cd release-artifacts
            find COMMIT_SHA python npm cratesio -type f -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum > SHA256SUMS
            sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
          )

      - name: Smoke-test exact Python distributions
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          shopt -s nullglob
          artifacts=(release-artifacts/python/abxbus-*.whl release-artifacts/python/abxbus-*.tar.gz)
          [[ "${#artifacts[@]}" -eq 2 ]]
          version="$(uv run --no-cache --no-project python -c 'import tomllib; print(tomllib.load(open("pyproject.toml", "rb"))["project"]["version"])')"
          for artifact in "${artifacts[@]}"; do
            smoke_env="$(mktemp -d)/.venv"
            uv venv --python 3.12 "$smoke_env"
            uv pip install --no-cache --python "$smoke_env" "$artifact"
            VIRTUAL_ENV="$smoke_env" uv run --no-cache --active --no-project python -c 'import importlib.metadata; import abxbus; assert importlib.metadata.version("abxbus") == __import__("sys").argv[1]' "$version"
          done

      - name: Smoke-test exact npm distribution
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          shopt -s nullglob
          npm_packages=(release-artifacts/npm/abxbus-*.tgz)
          [[ "${#npm_packages[@]}" -eq 1 ]]
          smoke_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
          cd "$smoke_dir"
          npm init --yes >/dev/null
          npm install --ignore-scripts "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/${npm_packages[0]}"
          node --input-type=module -e 'const pkg = await import("abxbus"); if (!pkg.EventBus) throw new Error("Missing ESM EventBus export")'
          node -e 'const pkg = require("abxbus"); if (!pkg.EventBus) throw new Error("Missing CJS EventBus export")'

      - name: Upload exact tested release artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: release-artifacts-${{ github.sha }}
          path: release-artifacts/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 90

name: test-go

on:
  workflow_call:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  find_go_tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      GO_TASKS: ${{ steps.lsgrep.outputs.GO_TASKS }}
      # [{ "kind": "test", "name": "eventbus", "package": "./tests", "test_regex": "^(TestEventBus)$" }, ...]
      GO_TEST_TASKS: ${{ steps.lsgrep.outputs.GO_TEST_TASKS }}
      # [{ "kind": "test", "name": "eventbus", ... }, ...]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      - id: lsgrep
        run: |
          GO_TEST_TASKS="$(
            find abxbus-go -type f -name '*_test.go' \
              | sort \
              | while read -r test_file; do
                dir="$(dirname "${test_file}")"
                rel_dir="${dir#abxbus-go}"
                if [[ -z "${rel_dir}" ]]; then
                  package="."
                else
                  package=".${rel_dir}"
                fi
                name="$(basename "${test_file}" _test.go)"
                test_regex="$(
                  sed -nE 's/^func (Test[A-Za-z0-9_]*)\(.*$/\1/p' "${test_file}" \
                    | paste -sd '|' -
                )"
                if [[ -z "${test_regex}" ]]; then
                  echo "No Test* functions found in ${test_file}" > /dev/stderr
                  exit 1
                fi
                jq -cn \
                  --arg kind "test" \
                  --arg name "${name}" \
                  --arg package "${package}" \
                  --arg test_regex "^(${test_regex})$" \
                  '{kind: $kind, name: $name, package: $package, test_regex: $test_regex}'
              done \
              | jq -s -c '.'
          )"

          echo "GO_TEST_TASKS=${GO_TEST_TASKS}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "GO_TASKS=${GO_TEST_TASKS}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "$GO_TEST_TASKS"
      - name: Check that at least one test file is found
        env:
          GO_TEST_TASKS: ${{ steps.lsgrep.outputs.GO_TEST_TASKS }}
        run: |
          if [[ -z "${GO_TEST_TASKS}" || "${GO_TEST_TASKS}" == "[]" ]]; then
            echo "Failed to find any *_test.go files in abxbus-go/" > /dev/stderr
            exit 1
          fi

  tests:
    needs:
      - find_go_tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        task: ${{ fromJson(needs.find_go_tests.outputs.GO_TASKS || '[{"kind":"error","name":"FAILED_TO_DISCOVER_TASKS"}]') }}
        # autodiscovers files in abxbus-go/**/*_test.go
        # - { kind: "test", name: "eventbus", package: "./tests", test_regex: "^(TestEventBus)$" }
        # - { kind: "test", name: "jsonschema", package: "./jsonschema", test_regex: "^(TestInferSchema)$" }
        # ... and more
    name: go-${{ matrix.task.kind }}-${{ matrix.task.name }}
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: abxbus-go
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Check that the previous step managed to find some tasks for us to run
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ matrix.task.kind }}" == "error" ]]; then
            echo "Failed get list of tasks from find_go_tests job" > /dev/stderr
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@40f1582b2485089dde7abd97c1529aa768e1baff # v5
        with:
          go-version-file: abxbus-go/go.mod
          cache: true
          cache-dependency-path: abxbus-go/go.sum

      - name: Set up Rust for cross-runtime roundtrip tests
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'test' && matrix.task.name == 'cross_runtime_roundtrip'
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4cda84d5c5c54efe2404f9d843567869ab1699d4 # stable
        with:
          toolchain: 1.97.1

      - name: Cache Cargo for cross-runtime roundtrip tests
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'test' && matrix.task.name == 'cross_runtime_roundtrip'
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32 # v2
        with:
          workspaces: abxbus-rust -> target

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@d0cc045d04ccac9d8b7881df0226f9e82c39688e # v6
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'test' && matrix.task.name == 'cross_runtime_roundtrip'
        with:
          version: "0.10.6"
          enable-cache: false
          activate-environment: true

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'test' && matrix.task.name == 'cross_runtime_roundtrip'
        with:
          version: 10.33.2

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'test' && matrix.task.name == 'cross_runtime_roundtrip'
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: abxbus-ts/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Install Go cross-runtime test dependencies
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'test' && matrix.task.name == 'cross_runtime_roundtrip'
        run: |
          cd ..
          uv sync --no-cache --dev --all-extras --no-extra tachyon
          pnpm --dir abxbus-ts install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run Go test file
        run: go test ${{ matrix.task.package }} -run '${{ matrix.task.test_regex }}' -p 1 -count=1 -timeout=600s

name: test-rust

on:
  workflow_call:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  find_rust_tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      RUST_TASKS: ${{ steps.lsgrep.outputs.RUST_TASKS }}
      # [{ "kind": "lib" | "test" | "bin", "name": "test_eventbus" }, ...]
      RUST_TEST_TASKS: ${{ steps.lsgrep.outputs.RUST_TEST_TASKS }}
      # [{ "kind": "test", "name": "test_eventbus" }, ...]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      - id: lsgrep
        run: |
          RUST_LIB_TASKS="$(jq -cn '[{kind: "lib", name: "lib"}]')"
          RUST_TEST_TASKS="$(
            find abxbus-rust/tests -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.rs' \
              | sort \
              | sed 's|^abxbus-rust/tests/||' \
              | sed 's|\.rs$||' \
              | jq -R -s -c 'split("\n")[:-1] | map({kind: "test", name: .})'
          )"
          RUST_BIN_TASKS="$(
            (
              if [[ -d abxbus-rust/src/bin ]]; then
                find abxbus-rust/src/bin -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.rs' | sort
              fi
            ) \
              | sed 's|^abxbus-rust/src/bin/||' \
              | sed 's|\.rs$||' \
              | jq -R -s -c 'split("\n")[:-1] | map({kind: "bin", name: .})'
          )"
          RUST_TASKS="$(jq -cn --argjson lib "$RUST_LIB_TASKS" --argjson tests "$RUST_TEST_TASKS" --argjson bins "$RUST_BIN_TASKS" '$lib + $tests + $bins')"

          echo "RUST_TEST_TASKS=${RUST_TEST_TASKS}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "RUST_TASKS=${RUST_TASKS}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "$RUST_TASKS"
      - name: Check that at least one test file is found
        run: |
          if [[ -z "${{ steps.lsgrep.outputs.RUST_TEST_TASKS }}" || "${{ steps.lsgrep.outputs.RUST_TEST_TASKS }}" == "[]" ]]; then
            echo "Failed to find any *.rs files in abxbus-rust/tests/ folder!" > /dev/stderr
            exit 1
          fi

  tests:
    needs:
      - find_rust_tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        task: ${{ fromJson(needs.find_rust_tests.outputs.RUST_TASKS || '[{"kind":"error","name":"FAILED_TO_DISCOVER_TASKS"}]') }}
        # autodiscovers files in abxbus-rust/tests/*.rs and abxbus-rust/src/bin/*.rs
        # - { kind: "lib", name: "lib" }
        # - { kind: "test", name: "test_eventbus" }
        # - { kind: "bin", name: "abxbus-rust-roundtrip" }
        # ... and more
    name: rust-${{ matrix.task.kind }}-${{ matrix.task.name }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: abxbus-rust
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Check that the previous step managed to find some tasks for us to run
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ matrix.task.kind }}" == "error" ]]; then
            echo "Failed get list of tasks from find_rust_tests job" > /dev/stderr
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4cda84d5c5c54efe2404f9d843567869ab1699d4 # stable
        with:
          toolchain: 1.97.1

      - name: Cache Cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32 # v2
        with:
          workspaces: abxbus-rust -> target

      - name: Set up Go for cross-runtime roundtrip tests
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'test' && matrix.task.name == 'test_cross_runtime_roundtrip'
        uses: actions/setup-go@40f1582b2485089dde7abd97c1529aa768e1baff # v5
        with:
          go-version-file: abxbus-go/go.mod
          cache: true
          cache-dependency-path: abxbus-go/go.sum

      - name: Run Rust library tests
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'lib'
        run: cargo test --locked --all-features --lib -- --nocapture --test-threads=1

      - name: Run Rust integration test
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'test'
        run: cargo test --locked --all-features --test ${{ matrix.task.name }} -- --nocapture --test-threads=1

      - name: Run Rust binary tests
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'bin'
        run: cargo test --locked --all-features --bin ${{ matrix.task.name }} -- --nocapture --test-threads=1

name: test-py
permissions:
  contents: read

on:
  workflow_call:

jobs:
  discover_python:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      PYTHON_TASKS: ${{ steps.discover.outputs.PYTHON_TASKS }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@d0cc045d04ccac9d8b7881df0226f9e82c39688e # v6
        with:
          version: "0.10.6"
          enable-cache: false
      - name: Discover Python tests and examples
        id: discover
        run: |
          uv run --no-cache --no-project python - <<'PY'
          import json
          import os
          from collections import Counter
          from itertools import cycle
          from pathlib import Path

          targets = (
              {"os": "ubuntu-24.04", "os_name": "linux", "python": "3.11"},
              {"os": "ubuntu-24.04", "os_name": "linux", "python": "3.12"},
              {"os": "ubuntu-24.04", "os_name": "linux", "python": "3.13"},
              {"os": "ubuntu-24.04", "os_name": "linux", "python": "3.14"},
              {"os": "macos-15", "os_name": "macOS", "python": "3.11"},
              {"os": "macos-15", "os_name": "macOS", "python": "3.12"},
              {"os": "macos-15", "os_name": "macOS", "python": "3.13"},
              {"os": "macos-15", "os_name": "macOS", "python": "3.14"},
          )
          discovered = [
              *(("test", path) for path in sorted(Path("tests").glob("test_*.py"))),
              *(("example", path) for path in sorted(Path("examples").glob("*.py"))),
              ("runtime", Path("tests/performance_runtime.py")),
          ]
          if not discovered or not all(path.is_file() for _, path in discovered):
              raise SystemExit("Python test/example discovery produced a missing or empty task list")

          matrix = []
          for (kind, path), target in zip(discovered, cycle(targets), strict=False):
              matrix.append(
                  {
                      "id": f"{kind}-{path.stem}",
                      "kind": kind,
                      "path": str(path),
                      "needs_cross_runtime": path == Path("tests/test_cross_runtime_roundtrip.py"),
                      **target,
                  },
              )

          assigned = Counter((item["kind"], item["path"]) for item in matrix)
          expected = Counter((kind, str(path)) for kind, path in discovered)
          if assigned != expected:
              raise SystemExit("Every Python test, example, and runtime task must be assigned exactly once")
          if {(item["os"], item["python"]) for item in matrix} != {
              (target["os"], target["python"]) for target in targets
          }:
              raise SystemExit("Python tasks must cover every supported OS/Python cell")

          with open(os.environ["GITHUB_OUTPUT"], "a", encoding="utf-8") as output:
              output.write(f"PYTHON_TASKS={json.dumps(matrix, separators=(',', ':'))}\n")
          PY

  tests:
    needs: discover_python
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.task.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        task: ${{ fromJson(needs.discover_python.outputs.PYTHON_TASKS) }}
    name: ${{ matrix.task.path }} / ${{ matrix.task.os_name }} / Python ${{ matrix.task.python }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.task.python }}

      - name: Set up Go for cross-runtime tests
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime
        uses: actions/setup-go@40f1582b2485089dde7abd97c1529aa768e1baff # v5
        with:
          go-version-file: abxbus-go/go.mod
          cache: true
          cache-dependency-path: abxbus-go/go.sum

      - name: Set up Rust for cross-runtime tests
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4cda84d5c5c54efe2404f9d843567869ab1699d4 # stable
        with:
          toolchain: 1.97.1

      - name: Cache Cargo for cross-runtime tests
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32 # v2
        with:
          workspaces: abxbus-rust -> target

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@d0cc045d04ccac9d8b7881df0226f9e82c39688e # v6
        with:
          version: "0.10.6"
          enable-cache: false
          activate-environment: true

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime
        with:
          version: 10.33.2

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: abxbus-ts/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Install bridge service binaries
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime && runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: awalsh128/cache-apt-pkgs-action@553a35bb8ebd9fcabcb1c9451aa4c98e1b4ca8a9 # v1.6.3
        with:
          packages: redis-server nats-server postgresql sqlite3 gcc-14 g++-14
          version: bridge-service-binaries-gcc14-v1
          execute_install_scripts: true

      - name: Install bridge service binaries
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime && runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: brew install redis nats-server postgresql@17 sqlite gcc@14

      - name: Configure bridge service binaries
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ runner.os }}" == "macOS" ]]; then
            PG_BINDIR="$(brew --prefix postgresql@17)/bin"
          else
            PG_INITDB_PATH="$(find /usr/lib/postgresql -type f -name initdb | head -n 1)"
            PG_BINDIR="$(dirname "${PG_INITDB_PATH}")"
          fi
          if [[ -z "${PG_BINDIR}" || ! -x "${PG_BINDIR}/initdb" || ! -x "${PG_BINDIR}/postgres" ]]; then
            echo "Failed to locate PostgreSQL binaries (initdb/postgres)" > /dev/stderr
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "${PG_BINDIR}" >> "${GITHUB_PATH}"
          export PATH="${PG_BINDIR}:${PATH}"

          redis-server --version
          nats-server --version
          initdb --version
          postgres --version
          sqlite3 --version
          gcc-14 --version
          g++-14 --version

      - run: uv sync --no-cache --dev --all-extras --no-extra tachyon

      - name: Install optional Tachyon peer for bridge tests
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime
        run: CC=gcc-14 CXX=g++-14 uv pip install --no-cache tachyon-ipc

      - name: Build TypeScript ESM bundle for cross-runtime roundtrip tests
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime
        run: |
          pnpm --dir abxbus-ts install --frozen-lockfile
          pnpm --dir abxbus-ts run build

      - name: Verify bridge optional Python deps
        if: matrix.task.needs_cross_runtime
        run: |
          uv run --no-cache python - <<'PY'
          import importlib
          modules = ['asyncpg', 'redis', 'nats', 'tachyon']
          for module in modules:
              importlib.import_module(module)
          print('optional bridge deps import OK')
          PY

      - name: Run discovered test with coverage
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'test'
        run: uv run --no-cache coverage run --parallel-mode --source=abxbus -m pytest "${{ matrix.task.path }}"

      - name: Run discovered example with coverage
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'example'
        run: uv run --no-cache coverage run --parallel-mode --source=abxbus "${{ matrix.task.path }}"

      - name: Run discovered performance runtime with coverage
        if: matrix.task.kind == 'runtime'
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          uv run --no-cache coverage run --parallel-mode --source=abxbus "${{ matrix.task.path }}" | tee python_perf.log
          cat python_perf.log >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Check coverage files
        if: always()
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          coverage_files=(.coverage*)
          [[ "${#coverage_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]]
          for coverage_file in "${coverage_files[@]}"; do
            echo "Found coverage file ($coverage_file), size: $(stat -f%z "$coverage_file" 2>/dev/null || stat -c%s "$coverage_file") bytes"
          done

      - name: Upload coverage data
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.task.id }}-${{ matrix.task.os_name }}-py${{ matrix.task.python }}
          path: |

title: EventBusMiddleware
description: Base middleware interface for EventBus lifecycle hooks.
---

`EventBusMiddleware` defines the middleware hook contract used by `EventBus` in both runtimes.

Rust core event dispatch does not expose a public middleware trait yet. Use handler wrappers or inspect `EventBus::to_json_value()` / event result state directly until Rust middleware parity lands.

## Interface

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

```python
from typing import Any
from abxbus import BaseEvent, EventBus, EventHandler, EventResult, EventStatus

class EventBusMiddleware:
    async def on_event_change(self, eventbus: EventBus, event: BaseEvent[Any], status: EventStatus) -> None:
        ...

    async def on_event_result_change(
        self,
        eventbus: EventBus,
        event: BaseEvent[Any],
        event_result: EventResult[Any],
        status: EventStatus,
    ) -> None:
        ...

    async def on_bus_handlers_change(self, eventbus: EventBus, handler: EventHandler, registered: bool) -> None:
        ...
```

## Lifecycle behavior

- `on_event_change` / `onEventChange` runs on event lifecycle transitions.
- `on_event_result_change` / `onEventResultChange` runs on handler-result lifecycle transitions.
- `on_bus_handlers_change` / `onBusHandlersChange` runs when handlers are added/removed.
- Hook `status` values are only `pending`, `started`, and `completed`.
- Handler failures are represented on `event_result.status == 'error'` and `event_result.error` when the hook status is `completed`.

## Custom middleware example

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

```python
from abxbus import EventBus, EventStatus
from abxbus.middlewares import EventBusMiddleware

class AnalyticsMiddleware(EventBusMiddleware):
    async def on_event_result_change(self, eventbus, event, event_result, status):
        if status != EventStatus.COMPLETED:
            return
        if event_result.status == 'error':
            return
        print(event.event_type, event_result.handler_name)

    async def on_bus_handlers_change(self, eventbus, handler, registered):
        action = 'registered' if registered else 'unregistered'
        print(eventbus.label, handler.id, action)

bus = EventBus('AppBus', middlewares=[AnalyticsMiddleware])
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="TypeScript">

```ts
import {
  BaseEvent,
  EventBus,
  type EventHandler,
  type EventResult,
  type EventStatus,
} from 'abxbus'
import type { EventBusMiddleware } from 'abxbus/middlewares'

class AnalyticsMiddleware implements EventBusMiddleware {
  async onEventResultChange(
    eventbus: EventBus,
    event: BaseEvent,
    event_result: EventResult,
    status: EventStatus
  ): Promise<void> {
    if (status !== 'completed') {
      return
    }
    if (event_result.status === 'error') {
      return
    }
    console.log(event.event_type, event_result.handler_name)
  }

  async onBusHandlersChange(eventbus: EventBus, handler: EventHandler, registered: boolean): Promise<void> {
    const action = registered ? 'registered' : 'unregistered'
    console.log(eventbus.label, handler.id, action)
  }
}

const bus = new EventBus('AppBus', { middlewares: [AnalyticsMiddleware] })
```

	eventbus *abxbus.EventBus,
	event *abxbus.BaseEvent,
	eventResult *abxbus.EventResult,

</Tab>
<Tab title="Rust">

- Rust middleware implementations are not exposed yet.

</Tab>

---
title: EventHistory
description: EventHistory ordered store API for lookup, retention, and trimming.
---

`EventHistory` is the ordered event store owned by each `EventBus` as `bus.event_history`.
Rust stores the same history inside `EventBus` runtime state and exposes it through `EventBus` history methods rather than a standalone public `EventHistory` type.

It is the canonical history backend in each runtime and exposes ordered access, lookup (`find`), and retention controls.

## Common fields

- `max_history_size`: max retained events (`None`/`null` means unbounded, `0` keeps only in-flight visibility)
- `max_history_drop`: whether to trim oldest entries when over limit
- Ordered mapping keyed by `event_id`

## Mapping interface

`EventHistory` behaves like an ordered mapping in Python/TypeScript; Go exposes equivalent explicit methods.

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

```python
from abxbus import EventHistory

history = EventHistory(max_history_size=100, max_history_drop=True)
history[event.event_id] = event

exists = event.event_id in history
loaded = history.get(event.event_id)
count = len(history)

for event_id, item in history.items():
    print(event_id, item.event_type)
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="TypeScript">

```ts
import { EventHistory } from 'abxbus'

const history = new EventHistory({ max_history_size: 100, max_history_drop: true })
history.set(event.event_id, event)

const exists = history.has(event.event_id)
const loaded = history.get(event.event_id)
const count = history.size

for (const [event_id, item] of history) {
  console.log(event_id, item.event_type)
}
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

```go
maxSize := 100
history := abxbus.NewEventHistory(&maxSize, true)
history.AddEvent(event)

exists := history.Has(event.EventID)
loaded := history.GetEvent(event.EventID)
count := history.Size()

for _, item := range history.Values() {
	fmt.Println(item.EventID, item.EventType)
}
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Rust">

```rust
let bus = EventBus::new_with_history(Some("HistoryBus".to_string()), Some(100), true);
let event = bus.emit(SomeEvent {
    ..Default::default()
});
block_on(event.now());

let count = bus.event_history_size();
let ids = bus.event_history_ids();
let loaded = bus.runtime_payload_for_test().get(&ids[0]).cloned();
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Accessor methods

All runtimes expose explicit accessors in addition to mapping methods where the language supports them.

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

- `add_event(event)`
- `get_event(event_id)`
- `remove_event(event_id)`
- `has_event(event_id)`
- `find(...)`
- `filter(...)`
- `trim_event_history(...)`

</Tab>
<Tab title="TypeScript">

- `addEvent(event)`
- `getEvent(event_id)`
- `removeEvent(event_id)`
- `hasEvent(event_id)`
- `find(...)`
- `filter(...)`
- `trimEventHistory(...)`

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

- `AddEvent(event)`
- `GetEvent(event_id)`
- `RemoveEvent(event_id)`
- `Has(event_id)`
- `Find(...)`
- `Filter(...)`
- `TrimEventHistory(...)`

</Tab>
<Tab title="Rust">

- `event_history_size()`
- `event_history_ids()`
- `find(...)`
- `filter(...)`
- `max_history_size()`
- `max_history_drop()`

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## `find(...)`

`EventHistory.find(...)` supports:

- event pattern (`'EventType'`, class, or `'*'`)
- `where` predicate filtering
- field equality filters (`**event_fields` in Python, options object fields in TypeScript)
- `past` / `future` windows
- `child_of` constraints

`EventBus.find(...)` delegates to `event_history.find(...)`. Future waiter ownership remains on `EventBus`; the bus injects the callback used for future waits.

## `filter(...)`

Same as `find(...)` but returns the list of all matching events (newest to oldest)
instead of just the first match. Accepts an additional `limit` argument to cap the
result count. `find(...)` is implemented as `filter(..., limit=1)` returning the first
result or `None` / `null`.

## Retention and trim methods

- `trim_event_history` / `trimEventHistory` applies configured retention policy.
- `on_remove` callbacks let the caller run cleanup side effects when history entries are removed.

## Constructor options

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

```python
history = EventHistory(max_history_size=100, max_history_drop=False)
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="TypeScript">

```ts
const history = new EventHistory({ max_history_size: 100, max_history_drop: false })
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

```go
maxSize := 100
history := abxbus.NewEventHistory(&maxSize, false)
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Rust">

```rust
let bus = EventBus::new_with_history(Some("HistoryBus".to_string()), Some(100), false);
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

title: OtelTracingMiddleware
description: Emit OpenTelemetry spans for events and handlers.
---

`OtelTracingMiddleware` creates event and handler spans with parent-child linking.

## Constructor params

- `tracer` / `Tracer`: optional explicit OpenTelemetry tracer instance.
- `trace_api`: optional explicit `opentelemetry.trace` module in Python/TypeScript.
- `root_span_attributes` / `RootSpanAttributes`: attributes added to top-level event spans.

## Setup with EventBus

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

```python
from abxbus import EventBus
from abxbus.middlewares import OtelTracingMiddleware

bus = EventBus(
    name='AppBus',
    middlewares=[OtelTracingMiddleware()],
)
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="TypeScript">

```ts
import { EventBus } from 'abxbus'
import { OtelTracingMiddleware } from 'abxbus/OtelTracingMiddleware'

const bus = new EventBus('AppBus', {
  middlewares: [new OtelTracingMiddleware()],
})
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

```go
// Not implemented in the core Go module.
// OpenTelemetry is intentionally not a required Go dependency.
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Rust">

```rust
// Not implemented in the Rust crate yet.
// Use typed event JSON serialization with an external transport for now.
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Setup with Sentry

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

```python
import sentry_sdk
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from sentry_sdk.integrations.opentelemetry import SentrySpanProcessor

from abxbus import EventBus
from abxbus.middlewares import OtelTracingMiddleware

sentry_sdk.init(
    dsn='https://<public>@<host>/<project>',
    traces_sample_rate=1.0,
)

provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(SentrySpanProcessor())
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)

bus = EventBus(
    name='AppBus',
    middlewares=[OtelTracingMiddleware()],
)
```

Install requirements:

```bash
pip install sentry-sdk opentelemetry-api opentelemetry-sdk
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Rust">

```rust
// Not implemented in the Rust crate yet.
// Wire tracing around typed handlers directly until Rust middleware parity lands.
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Behavior

- Starts an event span when an event starts and ends it on completion.
- Starts one child span per handler execution.
- Records handler exceptions on handler spans.
- Links child events to parent handler spans where available.
- With Sentry OpenTelemetry integration enabled, these spans are exported to Sentry performance traces.

title: RedisEventBridge
description: Forward events via Redis pub/sub channels.
---

`RedisEventBridge` publishes event payloads to a Redis channel and subscribes for inbound events on the same channel.

## Go support

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Go">

`RedisEventBridge` is not implemented in `abxbus-go` yet. Use [JSONLEventBridge](./bridge-jsonl) for the currently supported Go bridge.

</Tab>
<Tab title="Rust">

```rust
// Not implemented in the Rust crate yet.
// Use typed event JSON serialization with an external transport for now.
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Optional dependencies

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

Install the Redis extra (recommended):

```bash
pip install "abxbus[redis]"
```

Equivalent direct dependency install:

```bash
pip install redis
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="TypeScript">

Install the Redis client package:

```bash
npm install abxbus ioredis
```

This bridge is Node.js-only.

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

```go
// RedisEventBridge is not implemented in abxbus-go yet.
// Use JSONLEventBridge for the currently supported Go bridge.
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Rust">

```rust
// Not implemented in the Rust crate yet.
// Use typed events plus EventBus JSON serialization with an external transport for now.
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Constructor params

- `redis_url`: redis URL in the form `redis://user:pass@host:6379/<db>/<optional_channel>`
- `channel`: optional channel override (defaults to URL channel segment or `abxbus_events`)
- `name`: optional bridge label

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

```python
from abxbus.bridges import RedisEventBridge

bridge = RedisEventBridge(
    'redis://user:pass@localhost:6379/1/abxbus_events',
    name='RedisBridge',
)
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="TypeScript">

```ts
import { RedisEventBridge } from 'abxbus/bridges'

const bridge = new RedisEventBridge(
  'redis://user:pass@localhost:6379/1/abxbus_events',
  undefined,
  'RedisBridge'
)
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

```go
// RedisEventBridge is not implemented in abxbus-go yet.
// Use JSONLEventBridge for Go process-to-process bridge tests and deployments.
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Rust">

```rust
// Not implemented in the Rust crate yet.
// Use typed events plus EventBus JSON serialization with an external transport for now.
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Setup with a bus

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Python">

```python
from abxbus import EventBus
from abxbus.bridges import RedisEventBridge

bus = EventBus('AppBus')
bridge = RedisEventBridge('redis://localhost:6379/0/abxbus_events')

bus.on('*', bridge.emit)
bridge.on('*', bus.emit)
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="TypeScript">

```ts
import { EventBus } from 'abxbus'
import { RedisEventBridge } from 'abxbus/bridges'

const bus = new EventBus('AppBus')
const bridge = new RedisEventBridge('redis://localhost:6379/0/abxbus_events')

bus.on('*', bridge.emit)
bridge.on('*', bus.emit)
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Go">

```go
// RedisEventBridge is not implemented in abxbus-go yet.
// Use JSONLEventBridge for Go process-to-process bridge tests and deployments.
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="Rust">

```rust
// Not implemented in the Rust crate yet.
// Use typed events plus EventBus JSON serialization with an external transport for now.
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Behavior

- `emit(...)` publishes serialized event JSON to the configured Redis channel.
- `on(...)` subscribes handlers for inbound messages and auto-starts the Redis subscriber.
- Incoming messages are parsed into events, reset, then emitted on the bridge's internal bus.
- `close()` unsubscribes and closes Redis clients.
- Runtime requirements: Python needs `redis` (`redis.asyncio`), TypeScript needs `ioredis` and Node.js.

name: Release

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Release candidate, CI]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_sha:
        description: Exact main commit with verified release artifacts
        required: true
        type: string
      candidate_run_id:
        description: Successful release-candidate run containing the verified artifacts
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: release-main
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  candidate:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' && github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    outputs:
      ready: ${{ steps.verified.outputs.ready }}
      candidate_run_id: ${{ steps.verified.outputs.candidate_run_id }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
      - id: owner
        shell: bash
        env:
          RELEASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        run: |
          VERSION="$(sed -nE 's/^version = "([^"]+)".*/\1/p' pyproject.toml | head -n 1)"
          TARGET="$(git ls-remote origin "refs/tags/release-candidate/$VERSION" | awk '{print $1}')"
          BRANCH_SHA="$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)"
          [[ "$TARGET" == "$RELEASE_SHA" && "$BRANCH_SHA" == "$RELEASE_SHA" ]] && echo 'ready=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" || echo 'ready=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Require successful full CI for this commit
        id: verified
        if: steps.owner.outputs.ready == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          CANDIDATE_RUN_ID="$(gh run list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow release-candidate.yml \
            --commit "$RELEASE_SHA" --event push --limit 1 \
            --json databaseId,status,conclusion \
            --jq '.[0] | select(.status == "completed" and .conclusion == "success") | .databaseId // empty')"
          CI_RUN_ID="$(gh run list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ci.yml \
            --commit "$RELEASE_SHA" --event push --limit 1 \
            --json databaseId,status,conclusion \
            --jq '.[0] | select(.status == "completed" and .conclusion == "success") | .databaseId // empty')"
          [[ -n "$CANDIDATE_RUN_ID" && -n "$CI_RUN_ID" ]] || exit 0
          RELEASE_RUN_IDS="$(gh run list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow release.yml \
            --commit "$RELEASE_SHA" --limit 20 --json databaseId,status,conclusion \
            --jq '.[] | select(.status == "completed" and .conclusion == "success") | .databaseId')"
          while read -r RELEASE_RUN_ID; do
            [[ -n "$RELEASE_RUN_ID" ]] || continue
            PUBLISHED="$(gh run view "$RELEASE_RUN_ID" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json jobs \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.name == "publish" and .conclusion == "success") | .name')"
            [[ -z "$PUBLISHED" ]] || exit 0
          done <<< "$RELEASE_RUN_IDS"
          echo 'ready=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "candidate_run_id=$CANDIDATE_RUN_ID" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  dispatch-publish:
    needs: candidate
    if: needs.candidate.outputs.ready == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch the OIDC-compatible publish workflow
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_GH_TOKEN }}
          RELEASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          CANDIDATE_RUN_ID: ${{ needs.candidate.outputs.candidate_run_id }}
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          test -n "${GH_TOKEN:-}" || { echo 'RELEASE_GH_TOKEN is required to dispatch the trusted-publishing workflow' >&2; exit 1; }
          gh workflow run release.yml --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref main \
            -f release_sha="$RELEASE_SHA" \
            -f candidate_run_id="$CANDIDATE_RUN_ID"

  publish:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment: pypi
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}
      cascade_ready: ${{ steps.cascade-state.outputs.ready }}
    env:
      RELEASE_SHA: ${{ inputs.release_sha }}
      RELEASE_BRANCH: main
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ env.RELEASE_SHA }}

      - name: Revalidate release commit and tested runs
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CANDIDATE_RUN_ID: ${{ inputs.candidate_run_id }}
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          [[ "$RELEASE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
          [[ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" == "$RELEASE_SHA" ]]
          [[ "$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" == "$RELEASE_SHA" ]]
          VERSION="$(sed -nE 's/^version = "([^\"]+)".*/\1/p' pyproject.toml | head -n 1)"
          [[ -n "$VERSION" ]]
          [[ "$(git ls-remote origin "refs/tags/release-candidate/$VERSION" | cut -f1)" == "$RELEASE_SHA" ]]
          CANDIDATE="$(gh run view "$CANDIDATE_RUN_ID" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --json headSha,event,status,conclusion --jq '[.headSha,.event,.status,.conclusion]|@tsv')"
          [[ "$CANDIDATE" == "$RELEASE_SHA"$'\tpush\tcompleted\tsuccess' ]]
          CI_RUN_ID="$(gh run list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ci.yml \
            --commit "$RELEASE_SHA" --event push --limit 1 \
            --json databaseId,status,conclusion \
            --jq '.[0] | select(.status == "completed" and .conclusion == "success") | .databaseId // empty')"
          [[ -n "$CI_RUN_ID" ]]

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@d0cc045d04ccac9d8b7881df0226f9e82c39688e # v6
        with:
          version: "0.10.6"
          enable-cache: false

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4
        with:
          version: 10.33.2

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: 22.23.1
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: abxbus-ts/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Use npm with trusted publishing support
        run: npm install -g npm@12.0.1

      - name: Download exact tested release artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4
        with:
          name: release-artifacts-${{ env.RELEASE_SHA }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
          run-id: ${{ inputs.candidate_run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4cda84d5c5c54efe2404f9d843567869ab1699d4 # stable
        with:
          toolchain: 1.97.1

      - name: Authenticate with crates.io trusted publishing
        id: crates-auth
        uses: rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@c6f97d42243bad5fab37ca0427f495c86d5b1a18 # v1

      - name: Record verified release
        id: release
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          VERSION="$(sed -nE 's/^version = "([^"]+)".*/\1/p' pyproject.toml | head -n 1)"
          test -n "$VERSION"
          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Publish tested commit
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_GH_TOKEN || github.token }}
          RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ steps.crates-auth.outputs.token }}
        run: ./bin/release.sh

      - name: Confirm this tested commit owns the release tag
        id: cascade-state
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          TARGET=""
          while read -r sha _; do
            TARGET="$sha"
          done < <(git ls-remote origin "refs/tags/${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}")
          if [[ "$TARGET" == "$RELEASE_SHA" ]]; then
            echo "ready=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "ready=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  cascade:
    name: Cascade verified release
    needs: publish
    if: needs.publish.outputs.cascade_ready == 'true'
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    uses: ArchiveBox/monorepo/.github/workflows/cascade-release.yml@main
    with:
      upstream_package: abxbus
      upstream_version: ${{ needs.publish.outputs.version }}
      upstream_artifact_name: release-artifacts-${{ inputs.release_sha }}
      upstream_run_id: ${{ inputs.candidate_run_id }}
    secrets:
      release_token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_GH_TOKEN }}

title: PostgresEventBridge
description: Forward events using PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY plus table storage.
---

`PostgresEventBridge` stores event payloads in a Postgres table and uses `LISTEN/NOTIFY` for low-latency fanout.

## Behavior

- `emit(...)` upserts event payload data into the bridge table, then sends `NOTIFY` with the event id.
- `on(...)` registers inbound handlers and auto-starts listener startup.
- On notifications, the bridge fetches the full row payload, reconstructs an event, resets it, and emits locally.
- Columns are created on demand only for `event_*` fields.
- The full event JSON is stored in `event_payload` (not just non-`event_*` fields).
- `event_*` columns are also stored as flat mirrored fields for indexing/querying.
- Rehydration merges `event_payload` with `event_*` column values back into a flat event object.
- Runtime requirements: Python needs `asyncpg`, TypeScript needs `pg` and Node.js.
